findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole batch and can block cancellations permanently
findings.body:
All cancellations run sequentially inside a single try. If any `client.request` throws, the loop stops and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached. Prisma queries are lazy, so none of the queued deletes run, including those for batches SendGrid already cancelled successfully.

On the next cron run the same reminders are returned again. SendGrid rejects a second cancel for a batch that already has a status, so the same first reminder throws on every run. Every cancelled reminder after it in the list then never gets cancelled, and those emails go out until the stale row ages past `scheduledDate`.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch, delete the row right after a successful cancel, and treat an 'already cancelled' response as success.

findings.title: Reschedule uses immediate SendGrid cancellation, reintroducing the 100-pending-cancellation limit
findings.body:
Rescheduling calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)`, which immediately POSTs a cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends`. That is the call the PR description says fails once 100 cancellations are pending.

Reschedules are frequent. They will fill the pending-cancellation quota again, after which these cancels fail silently (errors are only logged) and the old booking's reminders are still sent. Workflow deletion and step deletion in `workflows.tsx` use the same immediate path, so they have the same problem.

The immediate path also never deletes the DB row or sets `cancelled`. On reschedule this leaves stale reminder rows attached to the old booking.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation misses reminders scheduled shortly after the booking is cancelled
findings.body:
Cancelling a booking now only sets `cancelled: true`. The real SendGrid cancel happens in the cron, which runs every 15 minutes.

If the booking is cancelled when its reminder is less than about 15 minutes from `sendAt`, the next cron run may come too late. SendGrid needs the cancel some minutes before send time, or the run may come after the send. The email is then delivered for a cancelled booking. Before this change the cancel was sent immediately.

Fix: cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is already inside the cron's one-hour window, and defer only reminders scheduled further out.

findings.title: Cancellation flag update is not awaited
findings.body:
`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `forEach` and never awaited. The DB write that sets `cancelled: true` is now the only thing that stops the email from being sent.

In a serverless or API-route environment the handler can return before these promises settle, and the update can be lost. Errors are also swallowed. The same fire-and-forget pattern is used in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` and in `workflows.tsx`.

Fix: collect the promises and await `Promise.all` before returning.
